Subject: Proof of compliance handoff: SOC2 evidence & pen-test mapping

Hi Kelly —

Thanks again for partnering with Redwood on the SOC2 evidence exchange for our mutual customer (ACME Financial). We need to pull together the pen-test artifacts and the evidence mapping to close out the audit pre-checks. To make sure we're aligned, could you confirm the following: 

1) Deliverables: redacted pen-test report (PDF), the raw findings manifest (CSV/JSON), screenshots/samples that map to control IDs, and a signed attestation letter from HexaSec confirming the redaction scope.

2) Exchange mechanism: we can accept either (a) an S3 presigned upload into our vendor bucket (we'll provide path and presign windows), or (b) a temporary folder in our Evidence Portal (link at the bottom). If you prefer, SFTP can be arranged but presigned uploads are quickest.

3) Redaction rules: remove customer-identifying IPs and PII; retain fuzzed identifiers so we can map test cases to SOC2 control IDs. We will need a short notes file describing what was redacted for each artifact.

4) Timeline: to meet the customer's audit dry run on Sep 1, we need artifacts in hand by EOD Aug 20. Is that feasible for HexaSec?

I've attached a short spec for the evidence package (SOC2-evidence-spec.pdf) that lists the control mapping template we use. If anything in the spec conflicts with HexaSec's standard practice, flag it and we can discuss.

Thanks — looking for a quick confirmation of preferred transfer mechanism and ETA.

Jonas
VP, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2-evidence-spec.pdf (application/pdf; 132 KB)

Kelly —

Appreciate the quick turn. Confirming what we agreed and adding file-level expectations so our audit team can process the package without back-and-forth: 

- Final upload target (presigned S3): https://evidence.redwood.com/portal/vendor-uploads/hexasec (we will provide presigned URLs for each file; each link valid for 48 hours).
- Required files (one ZIP per artifact set preferred):
  * hexasec-psr-redacted.pdf (redacted pen-test report)
  * hexasec-findings-manifest.csv or .json (mapping test_id -> severity -> control_id)
  * redaction-manifest.txt (human-readable list of redacted fields per file)
  * sha256sums.txt (checksums for all files)
  * attestation-signed.pdf (signed statement from HexaSec on redaction methodology)

- Naming convention: vendor-hexasec/YYYYMMDD_<artifact-type>_v1.zip (example: vendor-hexasec/20260819_psr-redacted_v1.zip)
- Retention: files will be retained in our evidence portal for 90 days and archived for 12 months per customer contract; if HexaSec needs a different retention policy, flag it now.
- Who to contact: procurement contact is procurement@redwood.ai (please include PO number in the manifest). Audit day contact: laura.bennett@redwood.ai.

Quote from your note: 
> We will upload to: vendor-hexasec/hexasec-202608/ (subject to your final path).

That works — we'll send presigned URLs for each expected filename by EOD Aug 16 (tomorrow). If you can commit to Aug 19 delivery, we'll mark this as green for the Sep 1 dry run.

Exchange instructions attached (exchange-instructions.txt).

Thanks,

Kelly / team —

Technical notes for the upload (quick checklist):

1) Presign windows:
   - Each presigned PUT will be valid for 48 hours. If an upload fails, request a new presign.
2) Filenames & manifest:
   - Use the naming convention Laura listed.
   - Provide sha256sum for each file; put all checksums in sha256sums.txt.
3) Large artifacts:
   - If any artifact is >250MB, split into chunked zips and include an index file (index.json) that lists parts and checksums.
4) Encryption / metadata:
   - Uploads must be encrypted in transit (HTTPS) and objects stored server-side encrypted (SSE-S3).
5) Verification step:
   - After upload, email laura.bennett@redwood.ai with the manifest URL and we will verify checksums and completeness within 4 business hours.

Forwarding an example manifest header below:
